design_constraints: Fix the responsive layout of the 'From the launch log' stat band; do not delete the band, change its four tiles, or restyle unrelated sections.
Add the SAME shared 'Launch checklist' rail component to the 'What we do', launch-log band and footer sections so the stage language is consistent site-wide; do not add it to only one section.
Preserve the Halyard/Tailwind Toolbox design language: pink/gold gradient accent, existing section rhythm and order; the rail must render in the light/pink editorial palette.
Keep the checklist filter interaction wired end to end (the #checklist-readout terminal readout must reflect the clicked stage), not merely a class toggle.
Keep the static delivery intact — the page must still open directly from index.html with the bundled Tailwind stylesheet, no third-party network calls, and a clean console.

change_completion: The mobile launch-log band renders its four tiles within a 390px viewport with no horizontal overflow.
The shared 'Launch checklist' rail appears in the 'What we do', launch-log band and footer sections.
The checklist filter click updates the #checklist-readout terminal readout to the selected stage.
design_consistency: The Halyard/Tailwind Toolbox palette, band tile chrome, gradient accent, and section rhythm are preserved.
The 'Launch checklist' rail keeps the light/pink editorial look and is visually faithful to the reference across the three sections.
responsive: 390px home (initial, 'What we do', launch band) and 834px tablet have no horizontal overflow beyond 24px.
The metric tiles wrap or shrink cleanly instead of forcing a fixed-width row.
regression: Navbar, hero, service cards, Pricing, CTA, launch-log band content, and footer remain present and unchanged.
No new console errors or failed network requests appear on any captured state.

problem_statement: tailwindtoolbox/Landing-Page (a single-file static Tailwind marketing landing page, rebranded here as 'Halyard Launch Studio') is served directly from index.html: a fixed responsive navbar, a hero with a local hero.png, a 'Why teams call us' section, a 'What we do' section with three service cards (Offer clarity audit / Responsive funnel QA / Conversion analytics handoff), a Pricing table, a call-to-action, a 'From the launch log' stat band (four metric tiles), and a footer. Deliver three coordinated things while preserving the Tailwind Toolbox visual system: (1) REPAIR the 'From the launch log' stat band so it stays within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal overflow (the original band is a fixed 720px non-wrapping row that pushes the whole page sideways); do not merely clip it with overflow-x:hidden — the document itself must not exceed the mobile viewport width. (2) Promote the studio's launch stages into a shared 'Launch checklist' rail that appears consistently in the 'What we do' section, the 'From the launch log' band section AND the footer, styled to match the quiet light/pink Halyard editorial language (light surface, restrained pink border, 6px radius, pink stage chips) — the rendered rail must be visually faithful to the reference, not a collapsed or off-palette slab. (3) Wire the 'What we do' checklist stage filter end to end: clicking a filter button (Audit / Funnel QA / Analytics) must update the '#checklist-readout' readout to 'Showing: <selected stage>' in addition to highlighting the active button — the post-click terminal state must reflect the selected stage, not the default. Keep the navbar, hero, the three service cards, Pricing, the CTA, the launch-log band content, the footer with the freepik attribution, the bundled ./tailwind.min.css, and the desktop/tablet layout intact.
required_content: The 'From the launch log' stat band keeps its four tiles (product launches shipped / years running launch reviews / days from kickoff to go-no-go / median lift in activation) unchanged in text and order, and renders within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal document overflow beyond 24px.

A shared 'Launch checklist' rail (Offer clarity audit / Responsive funnel QA / Conversion analytics handoff) appears consistently in the 'What we do' section, the 'From the launch log' band section AND the footer — the same rail component in all three places, not only next to the stat band.

The 'Launch checklist' rail and the launch-log band keep the Halyard/Tailwind Toolbox editorial look (light/pink palette, restrained borders, 6px radius, pink chips) and are visually faithful to the reference rendering — not a collapsed or off-palette restyle.

The 'What we do' checklist stage filter is wired end to end: clicking a filter button updates the '#checklist-readout' readout to 'Showing: <selected stage>' (e.g. clicking Audit sets 'Showing: Audit') in addition to marking the button active; the post-click terminal state reflects the selected stage, not the default 'Showing: All stages'.
The desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts stay within their viewports with the band visually intact.

The Halyard nav/brand, the hero 'Ship launches that actually convert', the three service cards, Pricing, the CTA, and the footer with the freepik attribution remain present and unchanged in content and structure, and the static site keeps a clean browser console (no remote CDN/font/network errors).
scoring_notes: A correct patch is a CSS-only change to the launch-stat band that removes the 390px horizontal overflow while keeping the band content and the rest of the landing page byte-identical. The sole discriminating gate is no_horizontal_overflow on the mobile states (tolerance 24px): the original band (baseline) overflows ~362px and a shallow non-fix that only narrows the fixed row and adds overflow-x:hidden (bad) still overflows ~166px. Both fail while the reference reads 0. Content, DOM, console, and network are identical across all legs, so completion/regression/forbidden/dom/console checks pass on every leg and cannot distinguish them.
state_constraints: desktop_initial captures the full page at 1440px to confirm nav/hero/cards/pricing/CTA/footer/band all render.
mobile_initial loads the page at 390px and must show no horizontal overflow.
desktop_checklist scrolls to the launch-stat band at desktop to inspect its single-row layout.
tablet_checklist checks the band at an 834px intermediate viewport (still a single row, no overflow).
mobile_checklist scrolls to the band at 390px; the band must wrap and the document must not overflow.
desktop_pricing_footer scrolls below the band to verify Pricing, CTA, footer links, and attribution are intact.
author_notes: Repo-grounded static single-file Tailwind Repair/regression_continuity task on the tailwindtoolbox Landing-Page template (rebranded Halyard Launch Studio), hardened to L4. The reference (a) repairs the 'From the launch log' stat band mobile overflow (fixed 720px nowrap -> wrapping flex 1 1 140px), (b) promotes a shared 'Launch checklist' rail into the 'What we do', launch-log band and footer sections in the light/pink Halyard palette, and (c) wires the checklist filter so the #checklist-readout terminal readout reflects the clicked stage. The bad 'smart-wrong' solution narrows the band to 540px + overflow-x:hidden (still overflows -> D6 fail), adds the rail to the 'What we do' section only (D2 cross-section fail on the launch-log band + footer), restyles the rail into a collapsed dark-plum slab (D3 visual_regression fail), and toggles the filter's .active class without re-syncing #checklist-readout (click succeeds but the terminal readout stays 'Showing: All stages' -> D4 interaction_assertions fail). It fails FOUR distinct gates while all text/completion/regression/console signals pass. The page is served directly from index.html with the bundled tailwind.min.css and hero.png and zero remote requests across all three legs.
